feature: Capture a frozen organism comparison, explore while writing, and save a dedicated field observation
changes: Capture one ready comparison of two distinct actual organisms of the same species. The captured birth records own copied trait, marker and parent arrays plus exact means and differences.
The captured observation identifies both organisms and their actual birth generations/islands separately from the captured viewing island, generation and seed.

The observation remains attached to the frozen pair while browsing, changing species, visiting recorded generations or clearing the current pin. A second capture requires saving or explicitly cancelling the open observation.
An optional reflection is bounded to 2000 characters. Cancelling discards only the local captured draft; replacement expeditions immediately suppress and clear captures and feedback.

Saving writes the frozen evidence and reflection to the dedicated archipelagoResidentComparison journal entry with a 12000-character investigative-note limit. Saving again updates that entry and preserves other investigation entries and handwritten notes.

Saved feedback receives focus without a live region and provides a direct action to open the field journal. Native controls and a responsive evidence view support keyboard use and the non-WebGL fallback.
scientificCorrectness: Saved evidence contains exact copied trait/marker arrays, raw arithmetic trait means, B-minus-A index points, parent IDs, actual birth origins and captured viewing context.
Genotype matches use unordered unrounded copies, so A/a and a/A match. Recorded copy order remains visible in the evidence.
The saved protocol describes two inspected birth records and explicitly states that the pair is not a random sample and that its selection path was not recorded.

A comparison of two organisms does not establish a population trend, an evolutionary cause, changes within one individual, or a breeding-success ranking. One neutral marker does not estimate genome-wide diversity.
Capturing and editing use local presentation state. Journal saving uses the existing progress-note path, without changing the world, history, RNG or primer.

validation.scope: Only the logged focused suites, two selected EvoLab golden checks and thirteen listed browser journeys are claimed; this is not a full repository test run.

focused.execution: Existing 32 checks and the new captured-observation suite ran separately. The final new-check count is parsed from its completed summary.

render.scope: Two selected EvoLab golden checks; skipped tests belong to the filtered render run.

browser.scope: Two new captured-observation journeys and all eleven existing comparison, field-card, archipelago and framing journeys.

translationDelta.baselineScope: The finalizer verifies its narrow artifact writes leave the current shared catalogs unchanged; unrelated collaborator edits are outside this claim.

validation.priorValidationReportScope: All existing validation reports, including pending reports, are excluded from outputs and checked for unchanged bytes across finalization.
validation.journalExportLimit: The full note appears in Journal display/print and readable copied text. The existing encoded Class Snapshot payload retains a 300-character ordinary-note summary.
